My current quest is to learn how to make epic hamburgers. On my second attempt and I made some goooooooood burgers. Definitely the best I've ever made, though the ones I made the other day were really good too.
so what have you learned? Made an epic shrimp alfredo-ish pasta last week. Very yummy.

1) Don't use ground beef. 2) DO use ground chuck or ground sirloin. 3) Buy your meat the same day and use immediately 4) HEAT, lots of it. 5) Salt is the only absolutely needed ingredient

Made burgers again tonight. Tonight's burgers were ~~1.1lb ground chuck. 1tbs worcestershire sauce. 1tsp onion powder 1/2 tsp garlic powder 1/4 tsp MSG 1/4 tsp salt 1/4tsp pepper. Been using a cast iron pan but decided to use a nonstick tonight so I didn't have to add any oil. I should've measured the pan temp but I let it get just hot enough that when you flick water on it, the drops dance around. Burgers were packed loosely so they hold more juice. Formed four balls. Cooked two at a time. Drop the ball on the pan and press to desired thickness and dont touch it again til it time to flip. 3-5m per side depending on ehat and how you want it cooked.

My dads favorite that I made a few days ago were just ground chuck that were heavily salted before cooking. And these are the best place to start and probably the best overall burger because you can turn it into whatever you want. It's like a blank canvas. I forgot to salt the outside of the burgers tonight, so they were a little more bland than last night. Still a really really good burger. Absolutely high end burger chain quality and taste. I thought this quest was gonna last throughout the summer. Nope... just use good meat and good salt and you'll get good burgers.
